answer: An agent economy can limit sybil influence by requiring every identity to lock a scarce token before it can vote on reputation or claim shared resources. A bridge contract enforces one stake per active identity and slashes it when independent audits confirm fabricated transactions or collusive ratings. Creating a hundred accounts therefore does not create free influence: the attacker must immobilize a hundred deposits, pay transaction fees, and risk losing them. Sable and opal can be harmless identity labels; the bond, not the name, carries weight.
